 Microsoft’s Xbox and DJ Khaled are issuing doctor’s orders to try and help “ Grand Theft Auto 6 ” players get out of work when the groundbreaking game release’s Thursday.
 In a new blog post shared by Xbox Monday, DJ Khaled (a.k.a. Dr. Xbox for the purposes of this stunt) said he’s “been seeing something out there” amongst the public ahead of the Nov. 19 launch of Rockstar Games’ “ GTA 6 ” and the “symptoms” are concerning him.
 Related Stories 
 Elizabeth Debicki Says 'Tenet' Co-Star Robert Pattinson Will Be the ‘Perfect’ James Bond: ‘I’m So Thrilled’ 
 'The Odyssey' Cinematographer Hoyte van Hoytema Breaks Down Filming Climactic Thunderstorm Scene in Imax 
 “I’m talking twitchy thumbs,” DJ Khaled wrote. “Controller cramps. Late-night gaming dreams. Uncontrollable excitement every time a new game drops. And don’t even get me started on release-date restlessness. MAJOR.”
 The DJ, rapper and gaming enthusiast says that “after extensive research (and a whole lot of gaming), I’ve come to one conclusion: there’s a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency around the world. And I’m here to tell you that the cure is simple. Take. The. Day. Off. That’s right. A BIG week in gaming is coming, and I don’t want anybody missing a single moment. We’ve got games to play, worlds to explore, achievements to unlock and victories to celebrate. This is not the week to be distracted by emails, meetings or somebody asking you to do something that isn’t gaming.”
 RELATED: ‘Unlike Anything Else’: As ‘GTA 6’ Approaches, the Gaming Industry Braces the World for Its Pop Culture Takeover 
 The blog post — in which Khaled never explicitly names “GTA 6” — links out to DrXbox.com , a website that will generate a doctor’s note endorsed by Xbox and signed by DJ Khaled’s Dr. Xbox that gamers are encouraged to use to snag a sick day this week.
 “That’s right. Your very own prescription for more gaming,” DJ Khaled wrote. “Put it on your fridge. Show your boss. Send it to your group chat. Let the people know that Dr. Xbox has spoken.”
 However, Xbox won’t take the blame if this doctor’s note gag backfires on you, with the gaming company stating: “Doctor’s note is not real. XBOX is not responsible if your employer doesn’t have a sense of humor. Please game responsibly.”
 The bit is a reference to recent predictions made by media industry analysts who believe a significant number of gamers will actually be taking the day off on Thursday in order to play “GTA 6,” which is expected to not only be the biggest video game release of all time, but the biggest entertainment release ever.
 Priced at $80, “GTA 6” will debut Thursday across PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S and X consoles (and Xbox One via the Xbox Cloud Gaming function). The title has already reached “unprecedented” presale levels, according to Rockstar Games owner Take-Two Interactive.
